structure: Alice mechanics: card = name + claim (+ image only where it carries), short causal connectors; an action figure with swappable heads in a toy-box ring; opening analogy (nodding at a plan decided last week) paid off in the outro (Monday meeting as rehearsal, booker answers next season)
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck about the psychology of professional wrestling. It is performed by a toy wrestling figure inside its toy box, for whoever happens to be there.
bestOfReason: Heads 1, 2, 3, 4: the gimmicks on one body; the jobber is his own head.
Selling 9, 13, 14, 11, 10: the craft of the lie, too much and too little.
Who decides 45, 46: booker and spot caller.
Audience 49, 30, 31, 53: camera, empty arena, fake crowd, armchair experts.
Reality 35, 55: the real injury and the police that hides it.

cues.cue: plastic click at every head swap

beats: Click. New head. Big Bad Brain Wrestling action figure: four heads, one job. Sell it.
Ever nodded in a meeting at a plan that was decided last week? Congratulations, you're in the business.

beats.text: The Babyface: high-flying moves because audiences cheer for that. A slave to approval.
The Heel: if they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener: you don't ask for it, which makes them want you more.

beats.pre: And the head that came in the box:
beats.text: The Jobber: you exist to make the other guy look good.
The Master Seller: maintain the illusion of peril. Limp to the ring. Make them believe.
The Thigh Slap: a loud sound suggests high impact. It's an audio lie.
The Stomp Punch: kinetic misdirection.
The Oversell Clown: reacting to an attack far beyond reality.
The No-Sell Monster: sit right back up just to prove how dangerous you are.
The Sacred Mask: the single biggest identifier. Never remove it.
The Booker, spider in suit moving wrestlers like marionettes: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.

beats.pre: In the ring, the real script:
beats.text: The Spot Caller: a basic outline, filled in with sweat.
The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.
The Empty Arena: pausing for a pop that never comes.
The Green Screen Crowd: audio sweetening on a lie.
The Internet Smark: fans talking about psychology without ever taking a bump.
The Real Injury: unplanned. The crowd goes nuts because it's real.
The Kayfabe Police: keep the secrets secret, or get fired.
The Finisher: the Leg Drop. If this hits, go home.
The False Finish: the art of the near-fall.
The Retirement Match: rising, and falling. See you next season.

beats: Same show on Monday: the plan was booked last week, the meeting is the rehearsal, and somebody nods on cue to make the boss look good.
Questions are welcome, of course. The booker answers them next season.
